consult.text:
It sounds painful to have a daughter who has gone quiet and shut her door. You were worried about her, and now you feel shut out.

Here is how she may see it. Her diary was a private place. She may feel that her mother read it without asking, and then that something very personal was passed on to her aunt and grandmother. When it became a joke at a family dinner in front of everyone, she may have felt exposed and unable to trust you. Going silent could be how she protects herself, rather than drama.

The main issue here seems to be that her private diary was read and what she wrote was shared with other family members. Your worry was real, but those two actions are most likely what she is reacting to. Your sister's joke made it worse, but you are the one who told her.

We do not know what your daughter has said about it, or how she feels about being open with the family.

Some next steps:
1. Tell her you read the diary and shared it, that it was a breach of her privacy, and that you are sorry. Do not explain yet.
2. Ask what she needs from you and the family, and accept a slow answer.
3. Tell your sister and your mother not to bring it up again.
I'm her mother, I have a right to know what's going on in her life.

I understand. You love her, and not knowing what is happening with her is frightening. Wanting to be close to your daughter is a good thing to want.

I would still put the main point the same way. What seems to have hurt her most is that her diary was read and that what she wrote was passed on. She may need to see that you understand this before she can talk with you about anything else. Closeness usually comes back when she decides to share, rather than when it is taken.

Some steps:
1. Choose a calm moment, without an audience, to say plainly what you did and that you are sorry for it.
2. Offer to listen when she is ready, and let her set the pace. A short note under her door could be a gentle start.
3. Ask your sister and your mother to leave the subject alone, so she feels safe at home again.

share_draft: I read your diary, and I told Aunt and Grandma what I found. I should not have done either. It was your private space, and it was not mine to share. I am sorry. I also know what happened at the family dinner, and I understand why you have been keeping to your room. I miss talking with you. I would like to hear how this has been for you, whenever you feel ready. I will not push you, and I will not discuss what I read with anyone else.
